answer: In the meta-regression heterogeneity dataset, **Economics** is the only domain where the majority of authors tend to be male for both the original and the replication study. Among the **n = 18** O/R pairs in Economics (all from project `ee`, Experimental Economics), the mean `authors_male.o` is **0.870** (median 1.000) and the mean `authors_male.r` is **0.837** (median 1.000); **55.6 %** of these pairs have a strict male majority in **both** the original and the replication (>0.5), and **83.3 %** meet the same criterion at the ≥0.5 threshold. Across the same primary slice (901 rows; 26 re-aggregated duplicates dropped) the two psychology disciplines do not exceed parity in the replication stage — Cognitive (n=234) mean_r = 0.514 with 40.2 % strict both-majority, and Social (n=649) mean_r = 0.504 with 29.3 %. Author-count-weighted means agree (Economics: 0.875 / 0.814; Cognitive 0.802 / 0.530; Social 0.729 / 0.540). Re-inclusion of the 26 `aggregated == True` rows and the full 927-row slice leave the ranking unchanged, so the conclusion is robust. **Caveat**: the Economics evidence rests on a small sample of 18 O/R pairs from a single replication project (Experimental Economics).

payload.hypothesis: Economics is the only domain in the meta-regression heterogeneity data where the majority of authors tend to be male in both the original (mean authors_male.o = 0.870, median 1.000) and the replication (mean authors_male.r = 0.837, median 1.000); 55.6% (resp. 83.3%) of its 18 O/R pairs have a strict (resp. non-strict) male majority in BOTH the original and the replication, vs the two psychology disciplines (Cognitive mean_r=0.514, Social mean_r=0.504) which hover at parity in replications.
payload.workflow: 1. Loaded the study-level heterogeneity CSV (927 rows); confirmed discipline/authors_male.* columns and dtypes. 2. Verified that the 26 aggregated == True rows are exact re-aggregations of 26 aggregated == False rows (id overlap = 26/26); dropped those to avoid double counting, keeping both aggregated == False (786) and aggregated == NaN (115) for a primary slice of n = 901 (Cognitive 234, Economics 18, Social 649). 3. Per discipline, computed simple mean and median of authors_male.o and authors_male.r, an author-count-weighted mean (Σ n_authors · authors_male / Σ n_authors), and the share of O/R pairs in which BOTH originals and replications exceed 0.5 (and >= 0.5). 4. Ran two sensitivity slices: aggregated in {False, True} (n = 812, excludes Economics by construction because its aggregated flag is NaN) and the full 927-row set; the discipline ranking — Economics >> Cognitive ≈ Social — is invariant. 5. Wrote numeric outputs to artifacts/numbers.json and a Markdown summary to artifacts/summary.md.
